_comment: Copy this to skills/<your-skill>/evals/evals.json and replace the cases.
Delete this _comment block and the `note` fields once you are done.
The folder names the skill, so a case that should trigger it needs nothing
but an `id` and a `prompt`. Write the prompt the way a user would actually
type it -- copying phrases out of your SKILL.md description measures string
Tier 0 (required for every skill): at least 3 cases that should trigger
your skill and 2 that should not. Add `"expect_skill": null` for the ones
Tier 1 (required if your skill can be exercised on a generic runner): give
expectation, so something grades what the skill did and not just whether it
Tier 2 (hardware or a live service): add skills/<your-skill>/evals/machine.yml
so CI knows where to run it. Most skills do not need one.
Check your work without spending tokens:

cases.note: Positive. `expect_skill` is omitted because it defaults to this folder's skill.
cases.prompt: Something a user would say that should make this skill fire.
A different phrasing of the same need, with none of the same keywords.

cases.note: Tier 1. Same prompt grades routing AND what the agent then did.
cases.prompt: A task this skill should carry out end to end.
should: A thing the agent must do, in plain language, graded by an LLM judge
should_not: A mistake this skill exists to prevent

cases.note: Negative. Close to this skill's vocabulary but out of its scope: the wrong hardware, an adjacent domain, or a neighbouring skill's job.
cases.prompt: Something that sounds like this skill's territory but is not.
Another prompt that must not wake this skill up.
